title: Traverse book of John Davis's third voyage, 1587: page 50
creator: John Davis
description: A page of the traverse book kept on Davis's third voyage, ruled in columns for month, day, course, leagues run, latitude by observation, the wind, and remarks. This is the working navigational record behind the discovery of Davis Strait, printed by the Hakluyt Society from the original.

title: Traverse book of John Davis's third voyage, 1587: page 52
creator: John Davis
description: Traverse book columns for mid-July 1587, working north along the Greenland shore towards Sanderson's Hope, the farthest north Davis reached. Note the daily latitudes taken by observation and the plain remarks on ice and weather.

title: Traverse book of John Davis's third voyage, 1587: page 54
creator: John Davis
description: Traverse book columns for late July 1587: courses, leagues, latitude, wind, and remarks noting Mount Raleigh, the ice, and the fishing. A rare survival of an Elizabethan navigator's working table.

title: Traverse book of John Davis's third voyage, 1587: page 56
creator: John Davis
description: Traverse book columns for the crossing westward, with the remarks column recording the passage among the ice and the sighting of land.

title: Traverse book of John Davis's third voyage, 1587: page 58
creator: John Davis
description: The last traverse book pages of the 1587 voyage, running south towards the Labrador coast and home.

title: Title page of The Seaman's Secrets, John Davis, 1607 edition
creator: John Davis
description: Facsimile of the title page of Davis's own manual of navigation, first printed 1594: "The Seamans Secrets. Deuided into 2 partes, wherein is taught the three kindes of Sayling... Imprinted at London by Thomas Dawson."

title: Dedication of The Seaman's Secrets to Lord Charles Howard
creator: John Davis
description: The dedicatory epistle to the Lord High Admiral, with its decorated initial, opening Davis's navigation manual.

title: Full-page navigational diagram from The Seaman's Secrets
creator: John Davis
description: A full-page circular projection from the First Book of Davis's manual, laying out the sailings.

title: The compass of thirty-two points, The Seaman's Secrets p. 243
creator: John Davis
description: Davis's diagram of the mariner's compass with its thirty-two points named around the rose, illustrating the passage on sailing by compass "without any great errour".

title: Circular table for finding the Epact, The Seaman's Secrets p. 248
creator: John Davis
description: A ring diagram for computing the Epact, worked through in the text with the example of the year 1590 - part of the calendar arithmetic an Elizabethan navigator had to carry in his head.

title: Diagram of leagues sailed on every point of the compass, p. 256
creator: John Davis
description: The scale showing how many leagues are sailed upon each compass point to raise or lay a degree of latitude - the traverse table in geometric form.

title: Title page of the Second Part of The Seaman's Secrets
creator: John Davis
description: Facsimile of the divisional title: "The Second Parte of this Treatise of Navigation, wherein is taught the most excellent instrumen[t]s...".

title: The sphere of the world, The Seaman's Secrets p. 304
creator: John Davis
description: Armillary diagram of the sphere with its poles, axis, equinoctial and zodiac, from the passage on the poles of the zodiac.

title: The sphere of the world, second figure, p. 305
creator: John Davis
description: The companion armillary figure, showing the circles of the sphere as they stand to the horizon.

title: Projection of the cross-staff scale, p. 329
creator: John Davis
description: The geometric construction by which the degrees are projected on the transversary of the cross-staff.

title: Construction of the staff's degrees, p. 331
creator: John Davis
description: A second construction laying down the degrees from the intersections upon the staff.

title: A seaman taking an altitude with the back-staff, p. 332
creator: John Davis
description: Figure of an observer using the staff with his back to the sun - the Davis quadrant, the instrument that carried Davis's name at sea for two centuries.

title: A seaman observing with the quadrant, p. 334
creator: John Davis
description: Figure of an observer with the quadrant, near the close of the Second Book.

title: Circular demonstration and colophon, The Seaman's Secrets p. 337
creator: John Davis
description: The final circular demonstration of the staff, with the colophon "Imprinted at London by Thomas Dawson, dwelling neere the three Cranes in the Vintree, 1607".
